title: Trinity and Incarnation
welcome_lead: Step into the central mysteries of Christian theology: God as Trinity and the Incarnation of the Son.
meta_desc: Religious Studies Adventure: Trinity, Incarnation, Nicene and Apostles' Creeds.
final_note: You have walked the contours of Christian dogma. The creeds remain living confessions.

concepts.def: Christian doctrine of one God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
Doctrine that the eternal Son became human in Jesus of Nazareth (John 1).
Council of Chalcedon 451 affirmation of two natures, divine and human, in one person.

walkthroughs.body_html: The doctrine of the Trinity affirms that the Father, Son and Holy Spirit are distinct persons sharing one divine essence (ousia). Developed at Nicaea (325) against Arianism, articulated at Constantinople (381) and refined through the Cappadocian Fathers, it shapes worship and prayer.

The Council of Chalcedon (451) defined that Jesus Christ is one person in two natures, fully divine and fully human, without confusion or separation. Earlier debates rejected Arianism (Christ as creature) and Apollinarianism (only divine mind in a human body).

The Apostles' Creed and Nicene Creed remain central in Catholic, Orthodox, Anglican and many Protestant liturgies. The filioque clause — 'and the Son' added to the Western creed — contributed to the 1054 East-West schism and remains a point of ecumenical dialogue.
